newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end mostly off in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end mostly off in thin trade.

text.p: CME lumber futures showed little price direction and ranged mixed much of the day before closing mostly lower in continued thin trade, traders said.
Lumber closed unchanged to $1.40 per tbf lower with March off $1.00 at $405.80 and May unchanged at $382.00 per tbf.

Futures traded on both sides of previous levels after opening higher on support from a higher cash spruce quote. However, buying interest was light and prices eased at times as the market appeared to be awaiting the next move in the cash market. Trade was also light ahead of the holiday, traders said.

Secondary lumber supplies are called large in some areas of the country but in line with demand in others. Mills in the meantime are holding asking prices up in anticipation of increased business once weather conditions improve enough to get the spring home building season underway, they said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $408 per tbf, up $3 from midweek and up $12 from last Friday.
Futures will be closed Monday in observance of Presidents' Day and resume trading on Tuesday.
